questions.question: In 'pancreas divisum,' the majority of the pancreatic parenchyma drains through which duct?
choices: A. Duct of Wirsung into the major papilla
B. Duct of Santorini into the minor papilla
E. Accessory duct into the stomach
questions.detail: Divisum is the failure of the dorsal and ventral buds to fuse, meaning the larger dorsal duct (Santorini) handles most of the drainage.

questions.question: Annular pancreas in a neonate typically presents with:
choices: B. Duodenal obstruction and a 'double bubble' sign
questions.detail: The ring of tissue constricts the second portion of the duodenum, causing a proximal obstruction.

questions.question: Which finding is pathognomonic for 'chronic pancreatitis'?
choices: B. Calcifications in the distribution of the pancreatic duct
C. A solitary 2 cm cyst in the tail
E. Enlargement of the pancreatic head
questions.detail: Chronic ductal stones and calcification are specific hallmarks of chronic inflammation.

questions.question: 'Groove pancreatitis' occurs in the anatomical groove between the head of the pancreas and which two structures?
choices: B. Duodenum and Common Bile Duct
questions.detail: This focal form of pancreatitis mimics a head mass and involves this specific groove.

questions.question: The histopathologic hallmark of groove pancreatitis is:
choices: B. Fibrosis in the pancreatoduodenal groove
questions.detail: Chronic inflammation leads to dense fibrosis in this region.

questions.question: When evaluating a pancreatic neoplasm for resectability, which vessel's involvement is critical to assess?
questions.detail: Tumor contact or encasement of these major peripancreatic vessels determines if a surgical cure is possible.

questions.question: What percentage of pancreatic adenocarcinomas may be isoattenuating on portal venous phase CT?
questions.detail: A small percentage of tumors lack enough contrast difference from the normal gland to be easily seen.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a 'hypervascular' pancreatic lesion?
questions.detail: Most primary pancreatic malignancies are hypovascular, but neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) enhance avidly.

questions.question: An 'intrapancreatic accessory spleen' is a mimic of which pancreatic lesion?
questions.detail: Both can appear as hypervascular, well-circumscribed masses in the pancreatic tail.

questions.question: 'Fatty infiltration' of the pancreas can be caused by:
questions.detail: Multiple conditions lead to the replacement of pancreatic parenchyma with fat.

questions.question: Which pancreatic condition is associated with 'IgG4-mediated' autoimmune disease?
questions.detail: Autoimmune pancreatitis (AIP) is part of the IgG4-related systemic sclerosing diseases.

questions.question: Pancreatic 'atrophy' is a normal finding in which population?
questions.detail: Age-related volume loss is common and should be distinguished from pathologic atrophy.

questions.question: A 'pseudoaneurysm' in the pancreas is most often a complication of:
questions.detail: Inflammatory enzymes can erode adjacent arterial walls, leading to pseudoaneurysm formation.

questions.question: Main-duct IPMN is distinguished from side-branch IPMN by its:
choices: C. Lack of communication with the main duct
D. Location in the uncinate process only
questions.detail: Main-duct involvement is a high-risk feature for transformation to adenocarcinoma.

questions.question: The 'Double Duct Sign' refers to the simultaneous dilation of the:
choices: A. Common bile duct and cystic duct
B. Common bile duct and pancreatic duct
C. Right and left hepatic ducts
E. Portal vein and Hepatic artery
questions.detail: This typically indicates an obstructing mass in the pancreatic head or ampulla.
